clue.text: Earlier on page, short piece of text that's better than usual

parts.note: something earlier on a page is printed above

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a para is a paragraph, a piece of text

explanation.surface: A writer notes that an early, brief passage on the page is unusually good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims PARA to PAR. In golf, par is the expected score, so above par suggests better than the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being over the standard or normal level means exceeding what is expected, hence superior to the norm.

clue.text: Army officer organised air bridge

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the two words are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A military man sets up an airlift.
explanation.definitionFit: This rank sits above colonel in the British Army, so it names a senior military officer.

clue.text: From observers I only select one particular account

indicators.note: From tells us to take letters out of the words that follow
select says to pick a run of letters out of those words

explanation.surface: Of all the witnesses' statements, I choose just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering or telling of events from one point of view is a single account among several.

clue.text: Musician with piano in seaside entertainment location

indicators.note: with something in means the other piece is placed inside
with something in means the other piece is placed inside

parts.note: a pier is a British seaside structure with amusements and shows
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A performer brings a piano to the end-of-the-pier show.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the bagpipes or a pipe is a musician, as in the Pied Piper.

clue.text: Swift runner third in original Marathon, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: in the Greek alphabet, Marathon is spelt with rho as its third letter, which looks like a P

explanation.surface: A fast athlete came third in the first-ever Marathon, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' points to Marathon being a Greek place: in Greek letters the name starts M, A, rho. The roe deer is famously quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small, fleet-footed deer, so it is a swift runner.

clue.text: Four included in poll offered as promised

indicators.note: included in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a poll is a vote
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A number appears in election results offered as pledged.
explanation.definitionFit: A votive gift is given to fulfil a vow, so it is offered as promised.

clue.text: Acting for another cleric with promises of redemption

parts.note: a vicar is a parish cleric
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt, redeemed later

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers promises of salvation to his flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redemption' suggests salvation, but here it is paying off a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means done or felt on behalf of someone else, as a substitute.

clue.text: Isn't wet after changing a couple of garments

indicators.note: after changing means the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone stays dry once they change into a couple of fresh clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together, so it is two items of clothing.

clue.text: View is seen in a television set up

indicators.note: seen in means one piece appears inside the other
set up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A view is visible in a TV installed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the A and TV reading upward into VTA before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing long view or prospect, such as down an avenue.

clue.text: Bank in no-win situation, right?

parts.note: a tie is a draw, where neither side wins

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bank finds itself in a hopeless position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it means a row, as in banks of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, like a bank of seats rising one behind another.

clue.text: Extremely sanctimonious minister taking in a head

indicators.note: taking in means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
each means per head or apiece

explanation.surface: A clergyman being self-righteous takes on one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most inclined to moralise means being the most self-righteous, a superlative of moralising.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on one club as transport operator

parts.note: to tax is to strain or make heavy demands on
I is the Roman numeral for one
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A golfer strains one club while running a transport business.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbie runs a hired vehicle carrying passengers, so they operate a form of transport.

clue.text: Composer supported by court's judgment

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A composer has a court backing him in a legal ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's decision on a case is its finding or judgment.

clue.text: Control or influence over wife

indicators.note: over means the first piece covers or goes round the second

parts.note: having a say means having some influence

explanation.surface: A question of whether one has power or mere sway over a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'influence' looks like part of the definition but supplies SAY, wrapped round W.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have rule or command over something.

clue.text: Where one might get Brahms and Liszt?

definitions.text: Where one might get Brahms and Liszt?

parts.words: Where one might get Brahms and Liszt?
parts.note: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk; a bar with a pianist serves both drink and classical tunes

explanation.surface: A music lover wonders where to hear two Romantic composers.
explanation.walkthrough: The composers suggest a concert, but rhyming slang turns them into drunkenness, which a bar provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking venue with live keyboard music is where you might hear the composers or become tipsy.

clue.text: A Schubert composition for European city

indicators.note: composition means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A Schubert piece is written for a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Romania, a city in Europe.

clue.text: Production using available set

parts.note: a book that is out is on the market and available
to put is to set down or place

explanation.surface: A manufacturing line runs on a ready-made kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the amount produced, the yield of a factory or worker.

clue.text: Constant nuisance disturbed leader of government

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
leader of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A persistent pest has unsettled the head of the administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Never stopping means continuing all the time, which is being constant.

clue.text: Subject protecting monarch in hot spot

indicators.note: protecting means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A king's subject guards him in a dangerous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' suggests a monarch's subject, but it is a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot region of the globe, so a tropic stands loosely for a hot place.

clue.text: Fruit family put under grill

indicators.note: put under in a down clue means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: to pump someone is to question or grill them
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Fruit and relatives are set beneath a cooker grill.

clue.text: Popular attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: Someone cites a widely held opinion as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or occurrence offered as an illustration.

clue.text: A fool at Oval scored frenziedly

parts.note: git is British slang for a stupid person
O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: An idiot at the Oval cricket ground made runs in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, so 'scored' looks like batting; it means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction telling performers to play in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Menu item that computer user hasn't requested

definitions.meaning: a tinned luncheon meat that appears on cafe menus
unwanted bulk email sent to a computer user unasked

explanation.surface: A dish on the menu that the diner at the laptop never ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the canned pork product and unsolicited junk email.

clue.text: Day-labourer in North America last out of assembly plant

parts.note: a peon is an unskilled labourer in Latin America and the US

indicators.note: last out of means take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A casual worker in the US is last to leave the assembly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly plant' reads as a factory, but 'plant' is the definition, a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A peony is a garden plant with large showy flowers.

clue.text: Disappointing result of investing capital in bizarre times

indicators.note: investing means placing one piece inside another

parts.note: antic means grotesque or bizarre

Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A poor return comes from putting capital into the markets in strange times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing capital' sounds financial, but here investing just means putting a city inside other letters.

the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Goods are loaded at top speed onto an ancient ship.

clue.text: Arrest number one person responsible for financial oversight

parts.note: police book a suspect when charging them
the goalkeeper traditionally wears shirt number one

explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' suggests a leader, but it is the goalkeeper's shirt number.

clue.text: This stone is mine

definitions.meaning: the hard seed in a fruit such as a cherry

explanation.surface: A gem collector claims this stone as their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fruit's stone and a coal mine.

clue.text: Deer from Germany and Italy, originally

definitions.meaning: the chital, a spotted Asian deer
the alliance first formed by Germany and Italy in 1936, later joined by Japan

explanation.surface: A deer comes from two European countries at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spotted Indian deer and the wartime alliance of Germany and Italy.

clue.text: Sound made by seal in small pen, perhaps

clue.text: Rigorous, yet informally approximate
